articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Iran Designation Update
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced an Iran Designation Update on November 9, 2026.
This action is part of ongoing efforts to address activities deemed to be contrary to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests concerning Iran.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Iran-Related Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) implemented new Iran-related designations on November 6, 2026.
These designations target individuals and entities involved in activities that support the Iranian regime's destabilizing actions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Cyber-Related and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Issues Cuba Designations and Determination
body: On November 5, 2026, OFAC announced new designations targeting cyber-related and transnational criminal organizations, alongside new Cuba designations and the publication of a Cuba-related determination.

The U.S. Department of State designated eight entities and two individuals, and identified five vessels as blocked property under Executive Order 14404, which targets the Cuban regime's foreign military support and illicit revenue networks.

Additionally, OFAC issued a determination extending Executive Order 14404 to four more sectors of the Cuban economy: manufacturing, technology, electronics, and marine, paving the way for potential future sanctions in these areas.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / U.S. Department of State

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Iran-Related Designations, Updates, Alert, and Amended Venezuela General License
body: On November 4, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations, updates to certain Iran-related listings, and the publication of an Iran-related OFAC Alert.

The U.S. Treasury issued fresh sanctions against companies and individuals based in India and Turkey for their support of Iran, specifically targeting a vast criminal network involved in providing false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels transporting Iranian petroleum.
Additionally, OFAC issued an amended Venezuela-related General License and a related Frequently Asked Question, impacting transactions concerning the country.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-Related General License for International Development Bank Wind-Down
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued Iran General License FF-1 on October 29, 2026, which amends a previous Iran-related General License.

This amended license authorizes transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to wind down dealings involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, also known as Iraq Development Bank, and entities it owns 50 percent or more.
The wind-down period for these transactions is authorized through 12:01 a.m. eastern standard time on December 1, 2026.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Entities and Individuals Related to North Korea and Democratic Republic of the Congo
body: On October 28, 2026, OFAC announced new designations related to North Korea and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
These designations include individuals and entities tied to Russia, North Korea, and Rwanda, expanding restrictions that can impact financial institutions and cross-border transactions.
Among the designated entities is 'FIRST FINANCIAL AND TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENT CENTER,' listed in North Korea and Vladivostok, Russia, operating in financial and insurance activities.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Settles with OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. on October 27, 2026.

Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

The violations stemmed from the export of networking equipment and related services between September 2018 and March 2022 to a Russian defense manufacturer majority-owned by a designated Russian state-owned company, even though the manufacturer itself was not on the SDN List at the time of the transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: On October 26, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) amended several Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) as part of its ongoing review of published guidance.
The amendments cover FAQs related to blocking and rejecting transactions, as well as filing reports with OFAC, aiming to ensure that information remains current.

The updated FAQs clarify procedures for blocking accounts, handling interest on blocked funds, deducting service charges, and distinguishing between rejecting and blocking transactions, along with reporting requirements.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Sanctions Law Center

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related Designations, Belarus and North Korea Removals, and New General Licenses
body: On October 21, 2026, OFAC announced new Iran-related designations.
Concurrently, OFAC also announced designations removals related to Belarus and North Korea.
The action further included the issuance of new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses and amended Frequently Asked Questions.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues PAIPA Designations and Associated General Licenses
body: On October 19, 2026, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA).
These designations target foreign persons involved in significant theft of trade secrets of U.S. persons.

OFAC also issued PAIPA General License 1, authorizing transactions pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations, and PAIPA General License 2, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving certain entities blocked on October 19, 2026.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Fined Over $1.5 Million by OFAC for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle its potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to a Russian defense manufacturer that was majority-owned by a designated Russian state-owned company.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious and voluntarily self-disclosed, emphasizing the importance of sanctions-related diligence in acquisitions and oversight of foreign activities.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.
